text:
maria: Heads up — overnight we saw a cluster-level uptick in ECC/Xid noise. Fleet telemetry (last 90d) shows 9 permanent GPU replacements across ~1,800 cards. That implies ~0.17% failure rate per month (≈3 expected failures/month). Current global spare pool is 12 cards (0.67%). Thinking about whether we need to resize or reallocate by region — low-traffic regions would be fine with smaller share. Any quick math or triage suggestions?
cheng: thanks, digging in. Quick note: 9 replacements is 'permanent swap' after repeated Xid/ECC, not transient recoveries. I'm pulling per-region counts now (eu-west-1 has 5 of the 9).
andrew: quick sizing back-of-envelope: if expected failures λ≈3/month (fleet), Poisson variance ~λ so sqrt≈1.73. If we want a ~99% chance of not running out: s ≈ λ + 3*sqrt(λ) ≈ 3 + 3*1.73 ≈ 8.2 → round up to 9 spares. Current 12 seems fine globally but region skew matters.
sam_oncall: +1 for regional partitioning. eu-west has 5 failures in 90d => ~1.67/month there? Wait calculation: 5 failures / (90d) → 1.67 per 30d in eu-west? Let me be precise: 5/(90d)*30≈1.67/month. So eu-west expected λ_eu≈1.7/month. If eu-west pool is only 2 cards that's risky.
julie: Can we run a quick probability check for eu-west runout risk if spare_eu = 2 and λ=1.7? Using Poisson CDF: P(X>2)=1-P(X≤2). For λ=1.7, P(X≤2)≈0.89 → runout ~11%. That's too high for prod.
andrew: here's a tiny python snippet people can run locally:```python
import math
import mpmath as mp
lam=1.7
cdf=sum([mp.e**(-lam)*lam**k/mp.factorial(k) for k in range(0,3)])
print('runout_prob=',1-float(cdf))
```
maria: thanks. So if eu-west wants <2% chance of running out in a month, solve for s where P(X> s) < 0.02. For λ=1.7 that ends up s≈5 (quick check). We probably need to bump eu-west pool to 5.
cheng: agree. Also want to call out transient Xid spikes vs permanent hardware faults — we should only count replacements that needed RMA. I'll attach the raw event list in a follow-up.
devops-bot: [alert] gpu-eu-west ECC_error_rate > 75th percentile — 2024-11-07T02:13:12Z — flagged 7 cards with repeated Xid within 48h.
sam_oncall: action: increase eu-west spares by +3 from global pool (if available) and schedule a tech sweep of flagged machines. I'll open a ticket.
julie: ops question — do we keep spares pooled globally or regionally? My vote: regional minimums + global overflow. Eg: minimum 4 per region + global overflow 8. That meets putative 99% SLO for most regions.
andrew: also consider lead time for ordering new cards / warranty RMAs (2–4 weeks). If restock lead time L (weeks), we should size spares = expected failures over L + safety buffer. For L=3 weeks and λ_total≈3/month→ expected in L≈2.25 → spares ≈ 2.25 + 3*sqrt(2.25) ≈ 2.25+4.5≈6.75 → round to 7 for safety.
maria: TL;DR proposals: 1) Increase eu-west pool to 5 (move +3 if possible). 2) Set regional minimums: eu-west 5 (hot), others 3. 3) Global overflow pool 8. 4) Add Prom alert for sustained Xid_count>50 in 24h with automated pager for oncall. 5) Run deeper triage to separate soft ECC noise vs hardware RMAs.
cheng: +1 on separating soft vs hard. I'll post the event CSV. Assigning myself to triage and to update the runbook (replace vs retire thresholds).
sam_oncall: I'll create ticket INF-4821 to move spares and schedule the tech sweep. ETA EOD today for allocation change.
julie: also put a note to finance — moving spares across regions has minor egress/cost impacts and warranty transfers — I'll loop in procurement if we need to order more.
maria: perfect. If anyone wants the poisson/percentile table I computed, ping me and I'll paste it here. Thanks team :thumbsup:
